chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Washshāʾ, from Musāfir, that Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام said:
To him: “O Musāfir, are there fish in this canal?” He said, “Yes, may I be your ransom.”
So he said: “Indeed, I saw the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله last night, and he was saying: ‘O ʿAlī, what is with us is better for you.’”

key_terms.الْقَنَاةُ: the canal or water channel being referred to
key_terms.حِيتَانٌ: fish present in the water channel
key_terms.رَسُولَ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.مَا عِنْدَنَا: that which is with us, referring to the higher abode

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith indicate Imam al-Riḍā’s عليه السلام awareness of his approaching passing?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates a statement of Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام in which he recounts seeing the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله in a vision the previous night. The report indicates awareness of approaching death and conveys that what is with the Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله in the next world is better for Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Washha, from Musafir that, 
‘Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> said
him: ‘O Musafir! This (water) channel, are there fish therein?’ He said, ‘Yes, may I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>!’
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> saw Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> last night and he<sup>saww</sup> was saying: ‘What is with us<sup>saww</sup> is better for you<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha’ from Musafir that abu al-Hassan al-Rida (a.s.) said to him the following.
“O Musafir, in this water passage there is fish.” The narrator has said that he said, “Yes, “May Allah take my soul in service for your cause, there is fish there.”

The Imam (a.s.) then said, “I saw the Messenger of Allah last night and was saying, “O Ali, what is with us is better for you.” (The mention of fish is to show equality of degree of certain in his knowledge from observation and his knowledge from his dream.)
